newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees no signs of U.S. inflation heating up.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees no signs of U.S. inflation heating up.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Thursday that he does not see any signs of inflation heating up.
"I don't see evidence of it," he told reporters following a speech to a Treasury Department confernce on electronic money.
Rubin also said he expects Treasury to launch its first issue of inflation-indexed debt early next year.
Rubin pointed to a variety of reasons why he expects U.S. inflation to stay low -- large excess capacity in Europe, excess capacity in Japan, globalization and technological advances.
He called U.S. economic growth solid.
"Wages are going up, but inflation has not been reignited," he added.

Asked if that meant that the administration was at odds with the Federal Reserve, Rubin declined comment. Some Fed officials are pushing for higher U.S. interest rates because of fears that the pickup in wage growth will spur inflation.
Rubin said he saw a "fair chance" that Treasury's plan to issue inflation-indexed bonds might increase U.S. savings.
Treasury expects to announce "in the reasonably near future" the terms and other details of its first issue, he added.
That would pave the way for the first issue of the new type of debt early next year.
